style_when: the story turns on one physical thing — a part, a material, a component, a document — and what that thing costs, contains or crosses a border is the news
prompt: Extreme close-up macro photograph, 100mm lens, of a diamond solitaire ring lying at the edge of a narrow dark gap between two wide oak floorboards in a dim hallway. Single hard shaft of daylight from the left rakes across the pale wood, casting a long thin shadow; the ring is sharply focused, its facets glint, the floorboards and gap fall away into soft bokeh. Bone white, graphite, deep pine green; raw oak grain, polished platinum band. No text, no engraving, no labels. Extreme asymmetry, shallow depth of field, fine film grain.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, typography, letters, numbers, UI, watermark
rationale: The story turns on a single physical artifact—the ring—and the hidden financial gap beneath it. A 100mm macro photograph isolates the ring against the floorboard crevice, turning an abstract policy number into a visible physical gap without any text.
subject: a diamond solitaire ring lying at the edge of a dark gap between two oak floorboards
core_thesis: A contents limit is a stacked set of numbers where a category cap and theft-only peril sublimit leave a high-value item underinsured; only a scheduled rider lifts the cap.
core_conflict: The homeowner's expectation of full contents coverage versus the fine-print category sublimit and theft-only peril.
composition: extreme asymmetry with the ring at the left third, the floorboard gap running diagonally through the frame, and the right side falling into deep shadow

review.reason: The image depicts the exact object the article is about — a diamond ring sitting at the edge of a dark gap that stands in for the theft-limit coverage gap — so a reader would connect it directly to the headline's underinsured-jewelry claim.

input.prompt:
Extreme close-up macro photograph, 100mm lens, of a diamond solitaire ring lying at the edge of a narrow dark gap between two wide oak floorboards in a dim hallway. Single hard shaft of daylight from the left rakes across the pale wood, casting a long thin shadow; the ring is sharply focused, its facets glint, the floorboards and gap fall away into soft bokeh. Bone white, graphite, deep pine green; raw oak grain, polished platinum band. No text, no engraving, no labels. Extreme asymmetry, shallow depth of field, fine film grain.

Do not include: people, faces, hands, garbled text, random lettering, numbers, signage, watermarks, UI, logos.
